capitals.name: Kanchanaka (Nachna, Panna district)
capitals.note: Pravarasena I page: 'Pravarasena's capital was called Kanchanaka and has been identified with Nachna in the Panna district' (Bundelkhand). Coordinates are the district's approximate position. Start moved from 250 to 275 (repair 2026-10-19): Pravarasena I reigns c. 275-335 on his page, and neither the Pravarasena I page nor the Vakataka dynasty page names a seat for Vindhyashakti (250-270; the dynasty page: 'south Deccan, Madhya Pradesh and Malwa', Jayaswal's Bagat in the Jhansi district), so 250-274 has no capital dot. 335 is the end of Pravarasena I's reign; the page gives no date for the move south. The shape is corrected to reach Bundelkhand (vakataka-kingdom_260 and _306).

capitals.note: Nandivardhana-Pravarapura branch seat (the page: the Nandivardhana branch ruled from sites such as Pravarapura (Paunar), Mansar and Nandivardhana (Nagardhan)); the start year is the researcher's: the page's ruler table is garbled.

capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Vatsagulma (now Washim)': Sarvasena of the Vatsagulma branch 'set up his capital at Vatsagulma'; Harishena of that branch took over the Nandivardhana kingdom after Prithivishena II's death in 480.

correction.text: Vidarbha, the region of the later Vakataka seats at Nagardhan, Paunar and Washim: the page names no land for Vindhyashakti

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 250-259: the Vakataka dynasty is dated from Vindhyashakti (r. 250-270; infobox 'c. 250') but Cliopatria's first shape starts in 260. The page gives no land for Vindhyashakti, so only the Vidarbha core (the later seats of Nandivardhana, Pravarapura and Vatsagulma all lie in Vidarbha) is drawn until 259; the 260 shape (574,588 km2) is Cliopatria's. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Vakataka dynasty page says Vindhyashakti is 'placed variously at south Deccan, Madhya Pradesh and Malwa' (the Puranas make him ruler of Vidisha, 'but that is not considered to be correct') and that Jayaswal 'attributes Bagat, a village in the Jhansi district as the home of Vakatakas'; it does not mention Vidarbha. The Vidarbha core is the researcher's reading from the later seats and stays at confidence 1.

574,588 km2: Maharashtra 75%, Telangana 67%, Chhattisgarh 58%, Madhya Pradesh south, Karnataka north of the Tungabhadra, and 105 cells of Odisha. Pravarasena I page: his rule 'covered almost the whole of the Deccan between the Narmada and Krishna rivers' and 'his sphere of influence extended over Malwa, Gujarat, Andhradesha, and southern Koshala'; Vakataka page: from 'the southern edges of Malwa and Gujarat' to the Tungabhadra, from the Arabian Sea 'to the edges of Chhattisgarh'. The page gives no area; the shape is the Narmada-Krishna block without Malwa and Gujarat. The Odisha edge and Chhattisgarh interior are beyond the page's 'edges of Chhattisgarh'. The page ties the extent to Pravarasena I (r. 270-330), not to Vindhyashakti; the 260 start is Cliopatria's. Repair 2026-10-19 (reviewer): Cliopatria's 260 shape stops at 23.10 N, but the capital Kanchanaka (Nachna, 24.4 N 80.3 E, Panna district) of Pravarasena I (Pravarasena I page: 'Pravarasena's capital was called Kanchanaka and has been identified with Nachna') lies in Bundelkhand, 348 cells that no Cliopatria Vakataka shape contains. The Vakataka dynasty page: Pravarasena I (270-330) 'certainly ruled from Bundelkhand in the north' (Mirashi does not accept that he crossed the Narmada), and Vindhyashakti is 'placed variously at south Deccan, Madhya Pradesh and Malwa' with Jayaswal's Bagat, a village in the Jhansi district, as 'the home of Vakatakas'. The Bundelkhand part is drawn from 260 with the Cliopatria shape although Pravarasena I's reign opens in 275 on his page (270 on the dynasty page): for 260-274 it rests on Jayaswal's Bagat only (confidence 1).

Repair 2026-10-19 (reviewer): Bundelkhand (Nachna) added as for vakataka-kingdom_260; it holds to 335, the end of Pravarasena I's reign (c. 275-335 on his page, 270-330 on the dynasty page), and the new keyframe vakataka-kingdom_336 drops it for 336-346.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 336-346: the shape of 306 without Bundelkhand. Pravarasena I page: after his death 'these provinces seem to have become independent', 'Gautamiputra's son Rudrasena thus succeeded Pravarasena upon the latter's death' and 'Sarvasena founded a branch of the Vakataka dynasty at Vatsagulma'; the capital moves south to Nandivardhana in 336 (identity). The Cliopatria 347 shape (verdict ok below) lacks Bundelkhand, and a local king, Vyaghradeva of Nachna-Ganj, acknowledges Prithivishena I only from c. 360 (/ledger). The Gupta 347 shape covers 232 of Bundelkhand's 348 cells.

574,379 km2, same outline. Vakataka page: after Pravarasena I the kingdom divided into the Nandivardhana-Pravarapura and Vatsagulma branches (Sarvasena, r. c. 330-355, founded the Vatsagulma line); Cliopatria draws one state.

377,797 km2: -924 cells on 347 (Chhattisgarh and Odisha 345 to the Gupta shape, Karnataka and south Maharashtra 451 to the new Kadamba row, 35 to the Western Satraps). Prithivishena I page (r. c. 360-385): 'the Vakatakas under Prithivishena seem to have retained considerable influence in Central India', and the main branch's rulers came to be known as 'lords of Kuntala' after Vindhyasena's conquest of Kuntala (Vindhyasena c. 355-400 on the dynasty page); the Kadamba page has Kangavarma fighting 'the Vakataka might' c. 365. So Kuntala (north Karnataka, south Maharashtra) was contested between Vakataka and Kadamba; Cliopatria gives it to the Kadamba. Left as drawn (unverified: page budget); a vassal at Nachna (Bundelkhand) is recorded in the ledger, outside the shape.

378,158 km2, same outline as 353. Vakataka page: Rudrasena II (380-385) married Prabhavatigupta, who 'ruled as a regent on behalf of her two sons' for twenty years (385-405 on this page; c. 390-410 on the Chandragupta II page); Pravarasena II shifted the capital to Pravarapura.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the shape holds 451-461. 670,957 km2: +1,199 cells on 410, 1,019 of them Gupta land (Malwa, Mekala/Chhattisgarh, the Telangana edge). Narendrasena page (reign 'c. 455 - 480'): 'Around 445 CE ... he reclaimed his former capital by driving out the combined forces of the Guptas and Nalas'; 'The inscriptions of Prithivishena II ... assert that Narendrasena's authority was acknowledged by the rulers of Kosala, Mekala, and Malava', which many historians see as exaggeration; 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta'. Vakataka page: 'Under [Narendrasena] the Vakataka influence spread to some central Indian states.' The other 180 cells of the 1,199 (Maharashtra 132, mostly the Konkan coast and the northern Ghats at 18-19 N 73-74 E; Andhra 21, Chhattisgarh 16, Telangana 10) were nobody's Gupta land: they now have a gain event from nobody (repair 2026-10-19). Only the Chhattisgarh part has a page: the Narendrasena page says the campaign against the Nalas 'may have led to the further extension of Vakataka authority, especially in the area around present-day Chhattisgarh'; the page defines no frontier at the end of the reign. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F197: (1) the Aulikara core is subtracted from the Malwa gain: Narendrasena page (opened 2026-11-01): 'assert that Narendrasena's authority was acknowledged by the rulers of Kosala, Mekala, and Malava' is, in the page's words, an 'empty boast or exaggeration' of many historians' view; Aulikara dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01): the dynasty 'initially controlled the Malwa plateau' with Dashapura/Mandsaur as capital, so the Aulikara country is not Vakataka land even while 'Malwa' around it briefly was. 202 cells leave the shape; the 21 cells of the southern Malwa edge that Cliopatria's 410 shape already holds stay. (2) 'to' 461 is set: the entry text always said 'holds 451-461 only' but the compiler reads the shape's own years (451-475), so the 451 outline was unioned with the 462 keyframe and kept Malwa through 475 against the 462 keyframe's Skandagupta recapture.]

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the shape holds 490-510. 671,270 km2 with Malwa back (Harishena, c. 480-510). Harishena page: the Ajanta Cave 16 inscription of his minister Varahadeva describes 'the king's influence extending over many countries' (Kuntala, Avanti, Kalinga, Koshala, Lata, Andhra, Trikuta); Vakataka page, citing the Cave XVI inscription: he conquered Avanti (Malwa), Kosala (Chhattisgarh), Kalinga, Andhra, Lata (central and southern Gujarat), Trikuta (Nasik district) and Kuntala (southern Maharashtra). The shape reaches Avanti, Kosala and the Andhra interior, not Kalinga, Lata or Kuntala: those claims are influence, not holdings, and are not drawn. Ajanta Caves 16, 17 and 19 were excavated in his reign; 'the Vakataka dynasty came to an end not long after the death of Harishena' (Harishena page). [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F197: the Aulikara core is subtracted from the Malwa gain. Harishena page (opened 2026-11-01): the Ajanta inscription 'describes the king's influence extending over many countries' among them Avanti 'the region of western Malwa': influence, not possession, and the page names no Aulikara conquest; Aulikara dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01): the Chhoti Sadri inscription of 490 CE records Gauri as feudatory of Adityavardhana, an Aulikara house still on the Malwa plateau in 490, and Prakashadharma 'defeated the Huna ruler Toramana' (fl. 515-516). 202 cells leave the shape; the 21 southern-edge cells stay. The gupta-empire ledger/26 (not editable here) hands the same Malwa land to the Vakataka: see the report's handoffs.]

correction.text: years do not belong to the Vakataka state: the dynasty ends c. 510; the land passes to the Kalachuris of Mahishmati, the Kadambas, the Vishnukundinas and the Chalukyas

keyframe_review.note: The shape belongs to no year of the Vakataka state: the Vakataka infobox gives the end as c. 510 and the Harishena page says the dynasty 'came to an end not long after the death of Harishena' (about 510), with 'the Chalukyas of Badami' holding most of the former territory by about 550. Cliopatria keeps the Vakataka row to 554 and starts the Chalukya row in 555 over only 156 of its 2,688 cells. For 511-554 use the successors named in identity.successors.

The Vakataka infobox lists the Western Satraps among its predecessors; Cliopatria's Western Satraps shape drops 453 cells in 260 and the Vakataka shape starts at 574,588 km2. The page gives no date; the Narmada frontier is Pravarasena I's ('carried his arms to the Narmada in the north', reign c. 270-330). Re-read 2026-10-19: the Pravarasena I page dates his reign c. 275-335 and no campaign; the 260 year stays Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Deccan between the Narmada and the Krishna outside the Vidarbha core: Telangana, Maharashtra, the Chhattisgarh edge and northern Karnataka

ledger.note: c. 260: the rest of the 260 shape. Pravarasena I page: his rule 'covered almost the whole of the Deccan between the Narmada and Krishna rivers', with a sphere 'over Malwa, Gujarat, Andhradesha, and southern Koshala' and four Ashvamedhas; the dynasty page adds 'He annexed the kingdom of Purika which was being ruled by a king named Sisuka'. Cliopatria draws the full shape in 260, ten years before Pravarasena I's reign opens.

region.text: Bundelkhand (Panna district, Nachna): 'he certainly ruled from Bundelkhand in the north'

ledger.note: c. 260: Bundelkhand, the northern seat of the dynasty, is added to the Cliopatria shape. Vakataka dynasty page: Pravarasena I 'certainly ruled from Bundelkhand in the north' (the page gives his reign as 270-330, his own page c. 275-335); Pravarasena I page: capital Kanchanaka = Nachna, Panna district. The year is Cliopatria's start of the shape; the page dates no campaign and names no previous holder. Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding.

c. 336: Bundelkhand leaves the Vakataka shape. Pravarasena I page: at his death (c. 335) 'these provinces seem to have become independent', the Nandivardhana branch passes to Rudrasena I and Sarvasena founds the Vatsagulma branch; the capital moves south (identity). The page does not say who held Bundelkhand afterwards; a local king, Vyaghradeva of Nachna-Ganj, acknowledges Prithivishena I from c. 360 (/ledger). Cliopatria's 347 Vakataka shape lacks Bundelkhand. Bridge, not a dated event. Added 2026-10-19.

c. 353: Chhattisgarh and Odisha pass to the Gupta shape. Cliopatria's Vakataka shape drops 924 cells on 353, 345 to the Gupta. Samudragupta page: Mahendra of Kosala and Vyaghraraja of Mahakantara are among the Dakshinapatha kings he defeated; Prithivishena I page: the Vakatakas 'seem to have retained considerable influence in Central India'. No page dates the loss. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Prithivishena I page gives 'no territorial gains or losses with dates'; it says the Vakatakas 'seem to have retained considerable influence in Central India'. Stays confidence 1.

region.text: Kuntala: north Karnataka and south Maharashtra

ledger.note: c. 353: the south-west (north Karnataka and south Maharashtra) leaves the Vakataka shape for the new Kadamba row (451 cells). Kadamba page: Mayurasharma founded the kingdom c. 345 and Kangavarma (c. 365) 'had to fight the Vakataka might to protect his kingdom'; Prithivishena I page: Vindhyasena's conquest of Kuntala made the main branch 'lords of Kuntala'. The pages conflict on who held Kuntala; the Cliopatria drawing is kept. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Prithivishena I page is silent on the Kadambas and the Kuntala frontier ('Prithivishena likely provided material aid to Vindhyasena as the latter carried out the conquest of the Kuntala country'); the Vakataka dynasty page: Vindhyasena 'defeated the ruler of Kuntala, his southern neighbour'. Stays confidence 1.

region.text: Nachna and Ganj in Panna district, Bundelkhand

ledger.note: c. 360: Vyaghradeva of Nachna-Ganj acknowledges Prithivishena I. Prithivishena I page (r. c. 360-385): inscriptions found at Nachna and Ganj 'refer to a local king named Vyaghradeva who claims to have been a vassal of the Vakataka king Prithivishena'. The year is the reign's start; Bundelkhand is the researcher's reading of Nachna (Panna district).

region.text: Nachna and Ganj in Panna district, Bundelkhand

ledger.note: 385: Prithivishena I's reign ends and with it Vyaghradeva's claimed vassalage. The page dates the reign c. 360-385 and gives no later record; the end is bridged.

region.text: the Vakataka kingdom of the Deccan under the regent Prabhavatigupta

ledger.note: c. 390: the Vakataka kingdom under Prabhavatigupta's regency is 'practically a part of the Gupta empire'. Prabhavatigupta page (opened 2026-10-19): 'she effectively ruled the Vakataka Empire as regent from about 390 to 410' (infobox 'Regency: c. 390 - 410 CE'), her husband Rudrasena II died after 'only about five years' and 'Gupta influence over the Vakatakas reached its peak'. The Vakataka dynasty page dates the regency 385-405 and says the 'practically a part' view 'has no proper evidence'; the dates 390 and 410 are used here and in gupta-empire /ledger (mirror of its vassal_start and vassal_end). One scholarly reading, not a conquest. Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding.

region.text: the Vakataka kingdom of the Deccan

ledger.note: c. 410: the regency ends. Prabhavatigupta page: the regency ran 'from about 390 to 410'; Divakarasena 'never ascended' the throne and was succeeded by his younger brother Damodarasena (Pravarasena II) 'around 410' (the Vakataka dynasty page puts the regency at 385-405). Mirrors gupta-empire /ledger (vassal_end 410). Added 2026-10-19.

c. 445: Narendrasena drives the Guptas and Nalas from Nandivardhana. 'Around 445 CE, during the final years of Kumaragupta I's reign' he 'reclaimed his former capital by driving out the combined forces of the Guptas and Nalas'. Zone: the Gupta land Cliopatria hands to the Vakataka in 451.

c. 451: the Vakataka shape takes Gupta land in Malwa, Mekala and Kosala (1,019 cells). Narendrasena page: 'Narendrasena's authority was acknowledged by the rulers of Kosala, Mekala, and Malava' (an assertion 'many historians' see as exaggeration). Year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the 180 cells the 451 shape adds to the 410 shape outside the Gupta land of 443: the Konkan coast and northern Ghats of Maharashtra, an Andhra and Telangana edge and the Chhattisgarh edge

ledger.note: c. 451: 180 cells of Cliopatria's 451 shape (Maharashtra 132, Andhra 21, Chhattisgarh 16, Telangana 10) that were not Gupta land. Narendrasena page (r. c. 455-480): the campaign against the Nala king of Bastar 'may have led to the further extension of Vakataka authority, especially in the area around present-day Chhattisgarh'; 'Narendrasena's authority was acknowledged by the rulers of Kosala, Mekala, and Malava' (an exaggeration, many historians think); the page gives no frontier and no year for the extension, and says nothing of the Konkan coast. The cells lie beside no named state, so the counterpart is nobody. Added 2026-10-19 on the reviewer's finding (451 -> 410 had 180 unexplained cells).

c. 461: the contest ends with Skandagupta's recovery of Malwa. 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta'; the Skandagupta page's c. 460-461 inscription speaks of a 'tranquil reign'. Year bridged.

region.text: Malwa, the Gupta land the Vakataka held from c. 451

ledger.note: c. 461: Malwa returns to the Gupta. The Mekala and Kosala part stays Vakataka. 'Malwa wasn't under Vakataka for long as it was recaptured by Skandagupta' (Narendrasena page). Year bridged.

c. 480: the seat passes to Vatsagulma (Washim). Vakataka page: after Prithivishena II's death in 480 'his kingdom was probably annexed by Harishena of the Vatsagulma branch', the infobox capital being Vatsagulma.

region.text: Malwa (Avanti), the Gupta land the Vakataka held from c. 451

ledger.note: c. 490: Malwa returns to the Vakataka shape. Harishena page (r. c. 480-510): the minister Varahadeva's Ajanta inscription describes the king's influence over Avanti among other countries; Vakataka page, citing the Cave XVI inscription: he conquered Avanti (Malwa). Cliopatria's Vakataka shape of 490 is the 451 outline again. The Budhagupta page puts a Gupta governor between the Yamuna and the Narmada in 484-485; the Alchon Huns page has Toramana taking Malwa from the Guptas c. 510. Year bridged to the middle of Harishena's reign. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Ajanta Caves page gives Harishena as r. c. 475-c. 500 (and 460-477 elsewhere on the page), names none of his conquests and dates none; the year 490 stays a bridge to Harishena's reign. The Eran pillar and inscriptions keep eastern Malwa Gupta to 510 (see gupta-empire /ledger): this event gives the Vakataka western Malwa (Avanti, Ujjain) only.

region.text: the last Vakataka shape: Maharashtra, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh south of the Malwa edge, Chhattisgarh and the Andhra interior

ledger.note: c. 510: the Vakataka dynasty ends with Harishena. Infobox 'c. 250 to c. 510'; Harishena page: 'seems to have occurred very rapidly after Harishena's death in about 510', 'the Vakataka dynasty came to an end not long after the death of Harishena'; the Vakataka page: 'The end of the dynasty is unknown.' The Kalachuris of Mahishmati, the Kadambas and the Vishnukundinas take the lands; by about 550 the Chalukyas of Badami hold most.

wars.name: Pravarasena I's conquests
wars.outcome: Pravarasena I 'carried his arms to the Narmada in the north', annexed the kingdom of Purika and performed four Ashvamedhas; the page dates no campaign.
wars.note: Reign 270-330 on this page, c. 275-335 on the Pravarasena I page; 'No inscription or record from Pravarasena's reign has been discovered' (his page).

wars.name: Vakataka-Kadamba conflict over Kuntala
wars.outcome: Kangavarma (c. 365) 'had to fight the Vakataka might to protect his kingdom'; Bhageerath (c. 390) is said to have retrieved his father's losses, though the Vakataka inscriptions do not confirm it. Later marriage alliances: Kakusthavarma's daughter Ajitabhattarika married Narendrasena.
wars.note: Not a source of this dossier's keyframes: the Kadamba page is cited here for the war entry; the end year 435 is the accession of Kakusthavarma, bridged. No zone drawn: the pages do not say where the front lay. Re-read 2026-10-19: the Prithivishena I page does not mention the Kadambas; it has Prithivishena giving 'material aid to Vindhyasena as the latter carried out the conquest of the Kuntala country' and the main branch's rulers known as 'lords of Kuntala'. The Vakataka dynasty page: Vindhyasena 'defeated the ruler of Kuntala, his southern neighbour'; a Dashakumaracharita account has the Ashmaka ruler instigating the Kadamba ruler of Vanavasi to invade the Vakataka territory; a 519 Davanagere record implies the Kadambas annexed Vakataka land 'probably sometime after 500 CE'. No page draws the frontier.

wars.name: Narendrasena's war with the Guptas and Nalas
wars.outcome: Narendrasena retook Nandivardhana c. 445; Malwa recaptured by Skandagupta (undated).

wars.name: Prithivishena II against the Vishnukundinas
wars.outcome: Prithivishena II 'was defeated by the Vishnukundina king Madhava Varma II'; the page gives no date or land.

wars.name: Harishena's campaigns
wars.outcome: Harishena's minister's Ajanta inscription claims influence over Kuntala, Avanti, Kalinga, Koshala, Lata, Andhra and Trikuta; the drawn Vakataka shape reaches Avanti, Kosala and Andhra only.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line; the Narmada, the Tungabhadra and the Arabian Sea are the page's approximate limits. The eastern frontier at the edges of Chhattisgarh and the Kuntala frontier with the Kadambas are the least certain.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row, no split. Cliopatria ends it in 554; the pages end it c. 510 (infobox, Harishena page): the dossier ends 510 and marks the 546 shape wrong, the 490 shape adjust (years). Cliopatria draws no Kalachuri, Vishnukundina or Rajarsitulyakula row, so from 511 the northern and eastern Vakataka land has no state to receive it: those successors need dossiers (kalachuris-of-mahishmati, vishnukundina-dynasty); the Chalukya row (555) covers only 156 cells.
Page budget: 5 of 5 (Vakataka dynasty, Pravarasena I, Prithivishena I, Narendrasena, Harishena). The URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harishena_(Vakataka_dynasty) did not load (not found); the title 'Harishena' did. The Kadamba page (opened for the Kadamba dossier) is cited only in the war entry.
Unsettled: (1) Kuntala (north Karnataka, south Maharashtra): the Vakataka pages give it to Vindhyasena (c. 355-400) and the Kadamba page has Mayurasharma and Kangavarma holding Banavasi and the Malaprabha country; Cliopatria draws it Kadamba from 353; no contest is drawn because no page dates a campaign; (2) the dynasty page's ruler table is garbled (Pravarasena II is listed under the Vatsagulma line c. 400-415, yet the capital shift to Pravarapura is the main line's); the capital years 336, 400 and 480 are therefore the researcher's; (3) Harishena's claims over Kalinga, Lata, Andhra, Trikuta and Kuntala are influence, not drawn; (4) Prabhavatigupta's regency (385-405 here, c. 390-410 on the Chandragupta II page) is recorded as a Gupta vassal reading in gupta-empire; (5) Nachna's coordinates in the first capital are approximate.
The Cliopatria relation 'Alliance between Gupta Empire and Vakataka Kingdom' (324-554) starts at least 55 years before the marriage alliance the pages date (c. 380-390).
Gazetteer names needed: Kuntala (region), Nachna/Kanchanaka, Washim/Vatsagulma, Nandivardhana/Nagardhan, Pravarapura/Paunar (capitals only: coordinates given).

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) the 510 dissolve counterpart is kalachuris-of-mahishmati (applied by the reviewer; Vakataka page: 'probably defeated by the Kalachuri of Mahismati'). (2) Prabhavatigupta's regency is now a vassal pair with gupta-empire, 390-410 in both dossiers (Prabhavatigupta page: 'from about 390 to 410'); the Vakataka dynasty page's 385-405 is the other reading. (3) The capital Kanchanaka (Nachna) starts at 275 (Pravarasena I, c. 275-335); Vindhyashakti's seat is on no page (Bagat in Jhansi is 'the home of Vakatakas' per Jayaswal). Keyframes 260 and 306 add Bundelkhand (Vakataka dynasty page: Pravarasena I 'certainly ruled from Bundelkhand'); the new keyframe 336-346 drops it at the death of Pravarasena I (a bridge: ledger loss 336 to nobody). Gupta 347 covers 232 of Bundelkhand's 348 cells and Vyaghradeva's vassalage (360-385) lies inside; the Cliopatria Gupta sphere and the Vakataka claim overlap there. (4) 180 cells of the 451 shape had no event: a 451 gain from nobody (Konkan coast and northern Ghats mostly; only the Chhattisgarh edge has a page, Narendrasena: the Nala campaign 'may have led to' an extension). (5) Pages tried for the thin items: Pravarasena I (reign c. 275-335, no campaign dated), Prithivishena I (no gains or losses with dates; silent on the Kadambas), Ajanta Caves (Harishena r. c. 475-c. 500, no conquests named), Narendrasena (no frontier): the confidence-1 events stay at 1. Harishena's reign is c. 480-510 on his page and the Vakataka infobox, c. 475-c. 500 on the Ajanta page and 460-477 in another sentence of it: the 510 end rests on the infobox and the Harishena page. Counterparts needing dossiers: kalachuris-of-mahishmati, vishnukundina-dynasty, nala-dynasty (Bastar; belligerent of /wars/2 and the 451 Chhattisgarh gain).
